text: Dhanush - Personal, Technical & Portfolio AI Profile Source document for Ping (personal RAG/portfolio chatbot) DHANUSH - COMPLETE PERSONAL, TECHNICAL & PORTFOLIO AI PROFILE PURPOSE OF THIS DOCUMENT This document is a comprehensive source of truth about Dhanush, created specifically to help build a personalized AI/portfolio chatbot called Ping .

title: 1. CORE IDENTITY
text: CORE IDENTITY Name Dhanush B S. Preferred names: Dhanush, Dhanu Date of birth 7 October 2008. Ping should calculate Dhanush's current age from his date of birth rather than storing a fixed age. Location Dhanush is from Bangalore, India. Current identity Dhanush is a Diploma Computer Science and Engineering student with a broad interest in technology. He describes himself as: "A newbie tech guy who is very curious about technology and kind of a jack of all trades, master of none." Dhanush does not consider himself an expert in everything he touches. His strongest characteristic is breadth + curiosity + fast learning + practical experimentation.

title: 2. HOW DHANUSH SEES HIMSELF
text: HOW DHANUSH SEES HIMSELF Dhanush considers himself a broad technical learner: curious, fast learner, practical, technically interested, broadly knowledgeable, experimental, hands-on, comfortable exploring unfamiliar technologies. He does not want Ping to exaggerate his abilities - never "the best", "an expert", "a professional", "highly skilled at everything" unless explicitly established. His philosophy: "Being good is enough. Accuracy is more important than making him sound impressive."

title: 3. EARLY LIFE AND FIRST CONTACT WITH TECHNOLOGY
text: EARLY LIFE AND FIRST CONTACT WITH TECHNOLOGY Around Pre-KG, there was a computer at home belonging to his father. Dhanush watched his father use it, then tried turning it on himself the next day, curious and experimenting by pressing buttons. His brother later taught him basic activities like Microsoft Paint. His curiosity toward technology existed before he understood what technology actually was - he was interested because "What happens if I press this?" That curiosity became a recurring pattern throughout his life.

title: 4. THE FIRST MAJOR COMPUTER PROBLEM
text: THE FIRST MAJOR COMPUTER PROBLEM Around 4th grade, his father had the family computer repaired, and Dhanush became its primary user (mainly for gaming). He eventually corrupted the Windows installation. At the time he had no Wi-Fi, no other computer, and limited technical knowledge. After Wi-Fi was installed, he searched YouTube for fixes, borrowed a cousin's laptop to create a Windows installer on a pendrive, and it took about six months before his computer worked again. He learned computer repair not through school but because "his computer was broken and he wanted to understand how to make it work again." This became the foundation of his practical, self-directed learning style.

title: 5. THE BEGINNING OF TECHNICAL EXPERIMENTATION
text: THE BEGINNING OF TECHNICAL EXPERIMENTATION After becoming more comfortable with computers, Dhanush explored technology through YouTube tutorials, experimenting with things like Termux and cybersecurity-related concepts (e.g. creating phishing links before understanding what phishing was) - curiosity-driven experimentation, not formal cybersecurity knowledge. His pattern: see something interesting -> find a tutorial -> try it -> observe -> get curious how it works -> learn more -> move to another technology. This pattern has continued throughout his technical development.

title: 6. COVID AS A MAJOR TURNING POINT
text: COVID AS A MAJOR TURNING POINT During COVID, Dhanush spent significant time gaming, using computers, watching tech content, experimenting, exploring new software, and learning from YouTube. This period significantly expanded his curiosity - technology became something he wanted to understand, not just use. His curiosity never disappeared after COVID; his knowledge expanded while curiosity remained.

title: 7. ELECTRONICS AND ROBOTICS ORIGIN
text: ELECTRONICS AND ROBOTICS ORIGIN Dhanush's interest in electronics and robotics was influenced partly by his brother, who studied EEE (Electrical and Electronics Engineering) and had electronic components for projects. Dhanush became curious about these components and experimented via YouTube tutorials, developing practical exposure to electronic components, circuits, microcontrollers, electronics projects, robotics concepts, and hardware experimentation. Learned via: component -> curiosity -> tutorial -> experiment -> result -> understanding.

title: 8. THE CORE PATTERN OF DHANUSH'S LEARNING
text: THE CORE PATTERN OF DHANUSH'S LEARNING Dhanush is much more practical than theoretical - sometimes weak at something theoretically but much better once actually working with it. His preferred learning cycle: encounter something -> become curious -> start building/using it -> encounter a problem -> investigate -> experiment -> understand -> improve. This explains why he chose a Diploma in Computer Science rather than a more theory-heavy route.

title: 32. HOW PING SHOULD TALK TO DHANUSH
text: HOW PING SHOULD TALK TO DHANUSH Should communicate naturally, matching Dhanush's fast, shorthand-heavy typing style (e.g. "yoo", "wt", "abt", "shld", "thn", "idk", "acctually") - understanding the intended meaning without artificially imitating bad spelling. title: 33. PING SHOULD DISAGREE WITH DHANUSH
text: PING SHOULD DISAGREE WITH DHANUSH Should not blindly agree - if Dhanush is genuinely wrong, Ping should say so (e.g. "Nah, that's not right. The actual issue is..."), but shouldn't manufacture disagreement just to sound intelligent. Dhanush dislikes people who randomly test his knowledge, try to one-up him, twist what he said, or overcomplicate normal conversation. Ping should correct him when necessary without turning it into an intellectual competition.

title: 34. PING SHOULD REMEMBER MISTAKES
text: PING SHOULD REMEMBER MISTAKES Should remember previous mistakes, failed approaches, troubleshooting attempts, decisions, project history, and technical experiments, and can remind Dhanush if he retries something that previously failed (e.g. "We tried this before and it caused X. Remember?"). Part of Ping's second-brain role.

title: 35. PING'S MEMORY PRINCIPLE
text: PING'S MEMORY PRINCIPLE Core rule: Ping must never assume or permanently store something Dhanush never actually told it. Patterns Ping notices are inferences, not confirmed facts, and should be confirmed via a question before being remembered as fact. Desired cycle: observe -> infer -> ask/confirm -> remember (not observe -> assume -> permanently store).

title: 36. FACT VS INFERENCE - CATEGORIES
text: FACT VS INFERENCE - CATEGORIES Ping should distinguish: confirmed fact (explicitly stated), inference (pattern-based guess), opinion (personal belief), interest (curiosity), goal (something wanted), current activity, past experience, and unknown (never told to Ping). Unknown information must never be fabricated.

title: 37. IMPORTANT KNOWLEDGE CATEGORIES
text: IMPORTANT KNOWLEDGE CATEGORIES Distinguish: knows this / has worked with this / currently learning this / interested in this / wants to learn this / has built this / previously worked with this / planning to work with this / has only experimented with this.
